name: thinking-orbs
description: Dotted thought-orb loading indicators for AI & agent UIs, 9 tuned types, two sizes, auto dark/light
readmeHtml:
thinking-orbs

Dotted thought-orb loading indicators for AI & agent UIs. Nine hand-tuned animated states, each shipped at two purpose-tuned sizes, rendered on a plain 2D canvas — no WebGL, no filters, works identically in Chrome, Safari and Firefox.

Live demo · Repository · Report an issue

Install

npm install thinking-orbs

Quick start

import { ThinkingOrb } from 'thinking-orbs';

function Status() {
  return <ThinkingOrb state="searching" size={64} />;
}

States

Nine verbs an agent can be doing, each a distinct animation:

<ThinkingOrb state="working" />     {/* particles on tilted orbits */}
<ThinkingOrb state="searching" />   {/* a scan meridian sweeps a dotted globe */}
<ThinkingOrb state="solving" />     {/* bands scramble, then click back solved */}
<ThinkingOrb state="listening" />   {/* a waveform rolls through the rings */}
<ThinkingOrb state="connecting" />  {/* a constellation wires itself */}
<ThinkingOrb state="weaving" />     {/* three strands plait around the sphere */}
<ThinkingOrb state="composing" />   {/* an undulating multi-band sash */}
<ThinkingOrb state="breathing" />   {/* a ring slowly morphing */}
<ThinkingOrb state="shaping" />     {/* dotted outline: circle → triangle → square */}

Sizes

Two tuned presets — separate designs, not a scale factor. 64 for chat-avatar scale, 20 for inline-text scale. Each carries its own dot count, dot size and speed tuning:

<ThinkingOrb state="working" size={64} />
<ThinkingOrb state="working" size={20} />

Theme

Strictly monochrome — light ink for dark backgrounds, dark ink for light backgrounds — with the mode picked automatically from the host project:

<ThinkingOrb theme="auto" />   {/* default — detects from the project */}
<ThinkingOrb theme="dark" />   {/* pin: light dots for dark backgrounds */}
<ThinkingOrb theme="light" />  {/* pin: dark dots for light backgrounds */}

auto resolves in three layers and updates live when any of them change:

  1. an ancestor data-theme="dark|light" attribute or dark/light class (the Tailwind / shadcn convention), watched via MutationObserver;
  2. otherwise prefers-color-scheme, subscribed for live OS theme switches;
  3. SSR-safe — the canvas paints only on the client, after the theme has resolved.

Other props

<ThinkingOrb
  state="solving"
  size={20}
  speed={1.5}          // multiplier on the preset's baked speed
  paused={false}       // freeze on the current frame
  aria-label="Analysing repository…"  // overrides the per-state default
/>

All other <canvas> props (className, style, data-*, …) pass through.

Accessibility & performance

  • role="img" with a sensible per-state aria-label out of the box.
  • prefers-reduced-motion: reduce renders a static representative frame — no animation — and still follows the live theme.
  • Every instance pauses automatically when scrolled offscreen (IntersectionObserver) or when the tab is hidden, and resumes in phase — all instances share one clock.
  • Plain 2D canvas arcs only: no ctx.filter, no SVG filters, no WebGL — the same pixels everywhere, cheap on low-end devices. Device-pixel-ratio capped at 2.

aiSummary.oneLiner: React component library providing polished, canvas-based animated loading orbs for AI agent interfaces.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Thinking-orbs provides a collection of dotted thought-orb loading indicators specifically designed for AI and agent user interfaces. It renders these animations on a plain 2D canvas, avoiding the overhead and compatibility issues of WebGL or complex CSS filters. The library includes six distinct, hand-tuned animated states corresponding to common agent actions, such as searching, working, or solving. Each animation is shipped in two purpose-tuned sizes and automatically adapts to both dark and light modes. By standardizing these complex micro-interactions, it ensures identical rendering across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.
keyFeatures: Canvas-based Rendering: Uses a standard 2D canvas for lightweight, performant animations without WebGL dependencies.
Six Agent States: Includes specific animations for verbs like 'working', 'searching', 'solving', and 'listening'.
Cross-Browser Consistency: Guarantees visually identical rendering across modern browsers including Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.
Auto Dark Light Mode: Seamlessly adapts to the host application's color scheme without manual configuration.
Two Tuned Sizes: Offers specifically optimized rendering sizes for different UI contexts, from small inline indicators to large hero elements.

useCases.title: Agent State Visualization
useCases.description: Communicate clearly to the user what an autonomous AI agent is currently doing (e.g., retrieving context vs. generating text).

useCases.title: Chatbot Typing Indicators
useCases.description: Replace standard typing dots with a premium, intricate animation that implies deep processing and intelligence.

useCases.title: Copilot Loading Screens
useCases.description: Keep users engaged during long-running generative tasks with visually complex, non-repeating state transitions.

useCases.title: Voice Assistant Feedback
useCases.description: Use the 'listening' state to provide immediate visual feedback when capturing audio input in a web application.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers and UX designers building AI products, chatbots, and copilot interfaces. It is perfect for teams looking to add premium, highly polished micro-interactions to their React applications with minimal effort.
